title: Handwashing: The Cheapest Medicine
hook: It sounds almost too simple, but washing your hands well is one of the most effective things you can do to stop the spread of illness in a household.
key_points: Handwashing removes germs that cause respiratory and diarrheal illness.
Scrub with soap for at least 20 seconds, covering all surfaces of both hands.
Key moments: before eating or cooking, and after the toilet, coughing, or handling waste.
Soap and water beat hand sanitizer when hands are visibly dirty or greasy.
content_html: Of all the high-tech ways we fight disease, one of the most powerful is also the oldest and cheapest: soap, water, and twenty seconds. In a busy household, it's a frontline defense.
extra_html: The CDC calls handwashing a "do-it-yourself vaccine" because of how effectively it interrupts the spread of germs that cause respiratory infections and diarrheal illness. The method matters: wet your hands, lather with soap, and scrub all surfaces — backs of hands, between fingers, under nails — for at least 20 seconds before rinsing. The highest-value moments are before preparing or eating food and after using the toilet, coughing or sneezing, changing diapers, or handling garbage. When hands are visibly dirty or greasy, soap and water outperform alcohol-based sanitizer, which is a convenient backup rather than a replacement. In a household where one person's cold easily becomes everyone's, this single habit does an outsized amount of work.

source.name: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

related.title: Food Safety at Home
related.hook: Most food poisoning starts in an ordinary kitchen. Four simple habits — clean, separate, cook, chill — prevent the great majority of it.

related.title: Cold, Flu, or COVID?
related.hook: They share a lot of symptoms, but colds, flu, and COVID-19 differ in how fast they hit and how hard — and telling them apart can change what you do next.

flashcards.prompt: How long should you scrub with soap when washing your hands?
flashcards.explanation_html: The CDC recommends scrubbing all surfaces of your hands with soap for at least 20 seconds — about the time it takes to hum 'Happy Birthday' twice.

flashcards.prompt: When does soap and water beat hand sanitizer?
flashcards.back_html: When hands are visibly dirty or greasy. Sanitizer works on clean hands but doesn't remove grime or all types of germs.
